title: The spec-property-retirement playbook still instructs a `major` changeset, which ADR-0087's 2026-09-13 amendment superseded and check-changeset-no-major refuses
body:
## The contradiction, both sides quoted and line-numbered

Read first-hand on `origin/main` at 2026-09-20T13:55Z, ⛔ not on the shared checkout's working tree.

**The playbook**, `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md:291`, in its 面清单:

> - [ ] **Changeset** —— `@objectstack/spec` 用 `major`。AGENTS.md:breaking

**The contract that supersedes it**, `docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md:388-402`, 「Amended 2026-09-13 (#18003) — the level half」, landed by PR #18027:

> - **Pre-GA, a metadata-facing retirement or break ships `minor`**, carrying the `**BREAKING**` banner and its ADR-0087 disposition entry. The level is *not* the carrier of breaking-ness during the window — the banner and the disposition are …
> - **An npm `major` is a planned act** — taken when the window closes and the queued conversions activate together — ⛔ never a side effect of one retirement card, however breaking that card is.

Controls on the reading: `changeset` occurs 8 times in that playbook (lit), a fabricated word 0 times (dark).

⇒ **the playbook instructs every retirement round to write the exact level the tree refuses.** `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` exits non-zero on a `major`, so the failure is loud rather than silent — but it is a wasted lap every time, taken by the round that reads the playbook first.

## Why this is worth more than a one-line edit

⭐ **This card's own lane lost eight days to this fork.** Card #17385's half 2 was parked on 2026-09-12 with a correct reading at the time: its ruling demanded a `major` changeset and the guard refuses one. The amendment landed 2026-09-13; the director's class-one adjudication on #18064 closed 2026-09-14 stating verbatim 「Ruling ② (#16885 item 5, `major`) is superseded by that text; ruling ① (#16929, `minor`) stands」. Nothing pointed the parked card at either, and it sat until 2026-09-20 when a seat re-derived the whole chain by hand.

⇒ the playbook is the **first** thing a retirement round reads. Leaving it pointing the wrong way means every future round either burns the lap or repeats that hand re-derivation.

⚠️ **Also worth carrying into the fix, from the same amendment's third bullet:** 「A tombstone names the npm release it ships in, ⛔ never the protocol major.」 A round working from the playbook today gets no such instruction either. The live convention — already used by `metrics.zod.ts` and `tracing.zod.ts`, and followed by PR #19363 — is a tombstone saying `@objectstack/spec 17.5.0` while the migration entries are numbered at protocol 18. Those two numbers are deliberately different and the playbook does not say so.

## Class

**(b) — violating a declared contract**, with the contract text quoted above.

## ⛔ Not fixed here, and why

`.claude/**` is a governed surface. ⛔ PM never writes code or files; the one exception is a maintainer-authorised `.claude/` tooling PR, and there is no such authorisation for this. ⇒ filed for the `skills` lane to route and grade.
